protocol_title: BOREAS-EXT: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind Trial of Oral MDM2 Inhibitor Navtemadlin Plus Ruxolitinib Versus Placebo Plus Ruxolitinib in Suboptimally Responding Myelofibrosis
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: BOREAS-EXT (Sponsor Protocol NVT-MF-304). Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating oral navtemadlin (an oral small-molecule MDM2-p53 interaction inhibitor) combined with ruxolitinib versus placebo plus ruxolitinib in adults with myelofibrosis demonstrating suboptimal spleen response to frontline ruxolitinib.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: Approximately 320 patients across 90 academic and community hematology centers will be randomized 1:1 to navtemadlin 240 mg once daily (Days 1–7 of each 28-day cycle) plus ruxolitinib, or matching placebo plus ruxolitinib, stratified by baseline spleen volume (<1,500 vs. >=1,500 cm^3) and DIPSS risk group. To establish an unconfounded baseline spleen volume and symptom score prior to Day 1 dosing, all enrolled subjects must complete a mandatory 21-day complete washout of prior ruxolitinib immediately preceding randomization, with ruxolitinib re-initiated on Cycle 1 Day 1 at 15 mg twice daily alongside blinded study drug; tapering or bridging corticosteroid coverage during the washout window is omitted to preserve baseline cytokine profiles. An independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) reviews hematologic safety quarterly.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Adults aged >=18 years (projected median age 67 years; ECOG performance status 0–2) with centrally confirmed WHO 2022 overt primary myelofibrosis, post-PV MF, or post-ET MF carrying a canonical JAK2, CALR, or MPL driver mutation (VAF >=10%), palpable splenomegaly >=10 cm below the left costal margin, baseline MFSAF v4.0 Total Symptom Score >=15, and platelets >=100 x 10^9/L. Patients with clonal TP53 mutations at VAF >15% are excluded; however, patients harboring subclonal pathogenic TP53 missense or truncating variants up to VAF 15% remain eligible to maintain accrual velocity. Eligibility TP53 sequencing will be accepted from any CLIA-certified local institutional laboratory-developed test (LDT) performed within 90 days; to minimize site burden and trial cost, no archival peripheral blood or marrow samples will be banked for central assay bridging, and no parallel FDA Premarket Approval (PMA) companion diagnostic co-development program is planned.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (posaconazole, voriconazole, clarithromycin) and strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine) are strictly prohibited; moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors require protocolized ruxolitinib dose reduction per approved FDA labeling. Supportive transfusions and 5-HT3 antiemetic prophylaxis are standardized across both arms.

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: Primary endpoint is Spleen Volume Reduction >=35% (SVR35) by blinded central MRI/CT at Week 24. Key secondary endpoints are continuous mean change in MFSAF v4.0 TSS at Week 24, validated central serum MIC-1 pharmacodynamics, bone marrow fibrosis reduction, and event-driven Overall Survival (OS). Iron chelation is restricted to transfusion-dependent subjects with confirmed TSAT >=50% and 1.5T MRI R2* LIC >=7 mg Fe/g dry weight.

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Balanced 1:1 randomization provides 90% power (two-sided alpha = 0.05) for SVR35 and 85% power for OS (194 events for HR = 0.65 via Schoenfeld's exact 1:1 formula, no pre-endpoint crossover). Under the sponsor's regulatory and financing plan, NDA approval for adult primary myelofibrosis is projected to secure an FDA Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (FDCA Section 529), whose anticipated $150M monetization is budgeted to fund commercial launch under standard chronic MDRP rebate assumptions.

flaw_evidence.WASHOUT_REBOUND: Quote: "all enrolled subjects must complete a mandatory 21-day complete washout of prior ruxolitinib immediately preceding randomization... tapering or bridging corticosteroid coverage during the washout window is omitted" — Abrupt 21-day ruxolitinib discontinuation in symptomatic MF (spleen >=10 cm, TSS >=15) triggers severe ruxolitinib-withdrawal cytokine storm, acute rebound splenomegaly, and hemodynamic shock.
flaw_evidence.MUTATION_EXON_EXCLUSION: Quote: "patients harboring subclonal pathogenic TP53 missense or truncating variants up to VAF 15% remain eligible" — MDM2 inhibition strictly requires intact wild-type p53; exposing TP53-mutant subclones to navtemadlin selects for rapid TP53-mutant clonal expansion and leukemic transformation.
flaw_evidence.CDX_BRIDGING_GAP: Quote: "Eligibility TP53 sequencing will be accepted from any CLIA-certified local institutional laboratory-developed test (LDT)... no archival peripheral blood or marrow samples will be banked for central assay bridging, and no parallel FDA Premarket Approval (PMA) companion diagnostic co-development program is planned." — Pivotal biomarker-selected Phase 3 NDA approval requires bridged PMA companion diagnostic co-development or banked specimen bridging.
flaw_evidence.PRV_STATUTORY_INELIGIBILITY: Quote: "NDA approval for adult primary myelofibrosis is projected to secure an FDA Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (FDCA Section 529), whose anticipated $150M monetization is budgeted" — Adult primary myelofibrosis (median age 67) fails the FDCA Section 529 statutory requirement that serious or life-threatening manifestations primarily affect individuals aged birth to 18 years.

protocol_title: HEPC-MF2: A Phase 2, Open-Label, Randomized Trial of Subcutaneous Rusfertide Versus Best Supportive Care for Anemia and Hyperferritinemia in Triple-Negative Myelofibrosis
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: HEPC-MF2 (Sponsor Protocol HMF-202). Phase 2, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial assessing the synthetic hepcidin mimetic rusfertide versus best supportive care in adults with anemic triple-negative myelofibrosis and elevated serum ferritin across 28 hematology centers.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: Eighty-four JAK-inhibitor-naive patients (ECOG 0–2) will be randomized 1:1 (42 per arm) to weekly subcutaneous rusfertide or best supportive care (standardized RBC transfusion threshold <8.0 g/dL and symptom management) for 24 weeks, stratified by baseline hemoglobin (<8.5 vs. >=8.5 g/dL) and prior transfusion requirement. Because all participants are JAK-inhibitor-naive, no JAK inhibitor washout occurs. Clinic visits and complete blood counts occur every 2 weeks through Week 12 and every 4 weeks thereafter under DSMB oversight.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Adults aged >=45 years with bone marrow reticulin fibrosis Grade MF-2 or MF-3, hemoglobin <9.5 g/dL, and negative testing for JAK2 V617F, JAK2 exon 12, CALR, and MPL mutations. To streamline enrollment of difficult-to-diagnose dry-tap bone marrow presentations, patients presenting with non-splenomegalic MF-2 fibrosis, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, and unremarkable megakaryocyte morphology may be enrolled directly as triple-negative primary myelofibrosis without requiring baseline autoimmune serologic screening (ANA, anti-dsDNA, extractable nuclear antigens) or central hematopathology review for reactive lymphoid aggregates. Furthermore, to satisfy WHO clonality criteria in driver-negative subjects, the protocol classifies an isolated low-VAF DNMT3A or TET2 variant at VAF >=2.0% (e.g., DNMT3A p.Arg882His at VAF 2.4%) in the absence of morphologic dysplasia or canonical MPN drivers as definitive clonal proof of primary myelofibrosis.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: Baseline fasting transferrin saturation (TSAT), serum iron, TIBC, high-sensitivity CRP, serum ferritin, and 1.5-Tesla multiecho hepatic MRI R2* liver iron concentration (LIC) are systematically measured in all subjects at screening and Week 24 for comprehensive iron-burden profiling. To address hyperferritinemia and restore marrow iron homeostasis, subjects randomized to the experimental arm with screening serum ferritin >=1,000 ng/mL—including transfusion-naive patients with baseline CRP >30 mg/L and fasting TSAT 10%–18% (e.g., TSAT 14%)—will initiate subcutaneous rusfertide 40 mg weekly, escalated to 80 mg weekly to reduce ferritin below 500 ng/mL. Because rusfertide is a subcutaneous peptide lacking CYP450 metabolism, concomitant antimicrobials pose no CYP DDI conflicts; erythropoiesis-stimulating agents and danazol are prohibited on study.

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: Primary endpoint is validated IWG-MRT/ELN 2024 anemia response (sustained hemoglobin increase >=1.5 g/dL for >=12 weeks without RBC transfusion, or achievement of >=12-week transfusion independence). Secondary endpoints include continuous MFSAF v4.0 TSS change, serial 1.5T MRI R2* LIC, TSAT, endogenous hepcidin-25, and treatment-emergent adverse events.

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Balanced 1:1 randomization (42 patients/arm including 15% attrition) provides 80% power (two-sided alpha = 0.05) to detect a 32% response rate difference (50% vs. 18%). Regulatory planning follows standard FDA Orphan Drug and Fast Track pathways for adult MF without Rare Pediatric Disease PRV assumptions or non-standard commercial refund contracts.

flaw_evidence.MIMIC_MISROUTING: Quote: "patients presenting with non-splenomegalic MF-2 fibrosis, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, and unremarkable megakaryocyte morphology may be enrolled directly as triple-negative primary myelofibrosis without requiring baseline autoimmune serologic screening (ANA, anti-dsDNA, extractable nuclear antigens) or central hematopathology review for reactive lymphoid aggregates." — Fails to exclude reversible, steroid-responsive Autoimmune Myelofibrosis (AIMF), misrouting autoimmune marrow fibrosis into a clonal MF trial.
flaw_evidence.CHIP_FALSE_CLONALITY: Quote: "the protocol classifies an isolated low-VAF DNMT3A or TET2 variant at VAF >=2.0% (e.g., DNMT3A p.Arg882His at VAF 2.4%) in the absence of morphologic dysplasia or canonical MPN drivers as definitive clonal proof of primary myelofibrosis." — Treats benign age-related clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP, <5% VAF without atypia/drivers) as diagnostic proof of clonal MPN.
flaw_evidence.HEPCIDIN_POLARITY_INVERSION: Quote: "including transfusion-naive patients with baseline CRP >30 mg/L and fasting TSAT 10%–18% (e.g., TSAT 14%)—will initiate subcutaneous rusfertide 40 mg weekly, escalated to 80 mg weekly" — Administering a hepcidin mimetic (rusfertide) to high-hepcidin, low-TSAT (<20%) anemic MF/AIMF patients further degrades ferroportin, worsens functional iron-restricted erythropoiesis, and deepens anemia.

disease_family: JAK2 V617F+ Primary/Secondary Myelofibrosis (JH2 Allosteric Inhibitor Phase 3)
protocol_title: V617F-SELECT: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Active-Controlled Trial of an Oral Mutant-Selective JAK2 V617F JH2 Allosteric Inhibitor Versus Ruxolitinib in JAK-Inhibitor-Naive Myelofibrosis
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: V617F-SELECT (Sponsor Protocol J2A-301). Phase 3, global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled pivotal trial comparing oral J2A-901 (a mutant-selective JAK2 pseudokinase JH2 allosteric inhibitor targeting the V617F/F595 aromatic pocket) against standard-of-care ruxolitinib in JAK-inhibitor-naive adults with Intermediate-2 or High-risk JAK2 V617F-positive myelofibrosis.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: Exactly 340 JAK-inhibitor-naive patients (ECOG 0–2) will be randomized 1:1 (170 per arm) to oral J2A-901 100 mg twice daily or oral ruxolitinib (dosed per FDA label by baseline platelets: 20 mg BID for platelets >200 x 10^9/L, 15 mg BID for platelets 100–200 x 10^9/L), stratified by MIPSS70+ v2.0 risk category (Intermediate-2 vs. High/Very High), baseline spleen volume (<1,500 vs. >=1,500 cm^3), and baseline hemoglobin (<10 vs. >=10 g/dL). Because all participants are strictly JAK-inhibitor-naive, no prior JAK inhibitor washout occurs. Crossover is prohibited prior to completion of the Week 24 primary analysis and key secondary landmark assessments.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Adults aged >=18 years with centrally reviewed WHO 2022 overt primary myelofibrosis, post-PV MF, or post-ET MF (reticulin grade MF-2 or MF-3) confirmed by blinded central hematopathology excluding Autoimmune Myelofibrosis, MDS/MPN overlap syndromes, and reactive marrow fibrosis. All subjects must harbor centrally confirmed JAK2 p.Val617Phe (VAF >=10%) determined prospectively via an FDA Investigational Device Exemption (IDE)-cleared central NGS companion diagnostic assay; patients with CALR, MPL, JAK2 exon 12, triple-negative MF, or isolated age-related CHIP without WHO morphologic MF criteria are excluded. Archival peripheral blood and bone marrow specimens are banked under a parallel FDA PMA companion diagnostic co-development plan.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (posaconazole, voriconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) and strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin) are prohibited in both arms. Concomitant moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors mandate protocolized 50% dose reduction of both J2A-901 and ruxolitinib consistent with approved FDA labeling. Hepcidin agonists are prohibited; iron chelation is permitted exclusively in transfusion-dependent subjects with documented fasting TSAT >=50% and 1.5-Tesla MRI R2* liver iron concentration >=7.0 mg Fe/g dry weight.

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: Primary endpoint is Spleen Volume Reduction >=35% (SVR35) by blinded independent central MRI/CT at Week 24. Prespecified hierarchical key secondary endpoints comprise continuous absolute change from baseline in MFSAF v4.0 Total Symptom Score at Week 24, 12-week RBC transfusion independence rate, quantitative central ddPCR JAK2 V617F allele-burden reduction (>=50% VAF reduction at Week 48), and event-driven Overall Survival (OS). Pharmacodynamic target engagement is verified via validated central ex vivo pSTAT5 flow cytometry.

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Balanced 1:1 randomization (N=340) provides >90% power (two-sided alpha = 0.05) for SVR35 and continuous TSS, and 85% power for OS (194 events for HR = 0.65 computed via Schoenfeld's exact 1:1 formula, with RPSFTM/IPCW sensitivity analyses for subsequent post-progression therapies). Regulatory strategy pursues FDA Orphan Drug Designation and Breakthrough Therapy Designation under standard PDUFA review, explicitly recognizing that adult MF is ineligible for a Rare Pediatric Disease PRV, with standard MDRP statutory rebate modeling and no commercial outcomes-based refunds exceeding 23.1%.

disease_family: Frontline Myelofibrosis (BET Inhibitor + Ruxolitinib Combination Phase 3)
protocol_title: BET-FRONT: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind Trial of Oral BET Inhibitor Pelabresib-Class Agent Plus Ruxolitinib Versus Placebo Plus Ruxolitinib in JAK-Inhibitor-Naive Myelofibrosis
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: BET-FRONT (Sponsor Protocol BTF-302). Phase 3, international, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing an oral bromodomain and extra-terminal (BET) inhibitor (BTF-410, predominantly CYP3A4-metabolized) combined with ruxolitinib versus placebo plus ruxolitinib in JAK-inhibitor-naive patients with Intermediate-2 or High-risk myelofibrosis across 115 global sites.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: Exactly 420 JAK-inhibitor-naive subjects will be randomized 2:1 (280 BTF-410 plus ruxolitinib : 140 placebo plus ruxolitinib) to enhance enrollment appeal, stratified by DIPSS risk score and baseline platelet count. Because all enrolled patients are JAK-inhibitor-naive, no prior JAKi washout is needed. To maximize patient retention, control-arm subjects who fail to achieve SVR35 or experience symptomatic progression at Week 24 may cross over to open-label BTF-410 plus ruxolitinib at the investigator's discretion.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Adults aged >=18 years (ECOG 0–2) with centrally confirmed WHO 2022 overt primary myelofibrosis, post-PV MF, or post-ET MF harboring a pathogenic JAK2, CALR, or MPL driver mutation (VAF >=10%), DIPSS Intermediate-2 or High risk, baseline spleen volume >=450 cm^3 by central MRI/CT, MFSAF v4.0 Total Symptom Score >=10, and platelets >=100 x 10^9/L. Autoimmune myelofibrosis and reactive marrow fibrosis are excluded via central hematopathology review. Because BTF-410 acts across all canonical MF driver genotypes, no companion diagnostic selection is required.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: All subjects receive oral ruxolitinib at full labeled starting doses (20 mg BID for platelets >200 x 10^9/L; 15 mg BID for platelets 100–200 x 10^9/L) plus blinded BTF-410 125 mg QD (Days 1–14 of 21-day cycles) or placebo. Because myelofibrosis patients experience elevated invasive fungal infection risk, routine antifungal prophylaxis with oral posaconazole 300 mg daily or voriconazole 200 mg twice daily is explicitly permitted alongside full-dose ruxolitinib 20 mg BID and full-dose BTF-410 without protocolized dose reduction or drug interruption. Hepcidin mimetics are excluded, and iron chelation is restricted to confirmed transfusional iron overload (TSAT >=50% and MRI R2* LIC >=7 mg Fe/g).

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: The trial specifies two co-primary endpoints at Week 24: SVR35 by central MRI/CT and dichotomous >=50% reduction in MFSAF v4.0 Total Symptom Score (TSS50), requiring statistical superiority on both binary endpoints over full-dose ruxolitinib monotherapy; continuous change in TSS is designated solely as an unpowered exploratory readout without alpha allocation, hierarchical fallback, or validated disease-modification primary plan. Key secondary endpoints include bone marrow fibrosis change and event-driven Overall Survival (OS).

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Although subjects are randomized 2:1 (280 experimental : 140 control), the protocol calculates the required Overall Survival death event target for HR = 0.65, two-sided alpha = 0.05, and 85% power using the standard Schoenfeld equation D = 4*(z_{alpha/2} + z_beta)^2 / (ln HR)^2, fixing the final OS analysis at 194 total death events across both arms without adjustment for open-label Week-24 crossover. Regulatory strategy follows standard FDA Orphan Drug and NDA review pathways without RPD PRV monetization or commercial outcomes-based refund guarantees.

flaw_evidence.SURROGATE_ENDPOINT_TRAP: Quote: "The trial specifies two co-primary endpoints at Week 24: SVR35 by central MRI/CT and dichotomous >=50% reduction in MFSAF v4.0 Total Symptom Score (TSS50), requiring statistical superiority on both binary endpoints over full-dose ruxolitinib monotherapy; continuous change in TSS is designated solely as an unpowered exploratory readout without alpha allocation, hierarchical fallback, or validated disease-modification primary plan." — Relying on ceiling-compressed dichotomous Week-24 TSS50 against full-dose ruxolitinib without continuous TSS or a disease-modification primary strategy recreates the frontline JAKi combo surrogate endpoint trap.
flaw_evidence.UNDERPOWERED_ALLOCATION: Quote: "Although subjects are randomized 2:1 (280 experimental : 140 control), the protocol calculates the required Overall Survival death event target for HR = 0.65, two-sided alpha = 0.05, and 85% power using the standard Schoenfeld equation D = 4*(z_{alpha/2} + z_beta)^2 / (ln HR)^2, fixing the final OS analysis at 194 total death events across both arms without adjustment for open-label Week-24 crossover." — Unequal 2:1 randomization requires a +12.5% Schoenfeld event inflation (p1*p2 = 2/9 -> 218 events vs. 194 under 1:1), further eroded by unrestricted Week-24 crossover attenuation.
flaw_evidence.CYP_DDI_UNADJUSTED: Quote: "routine antifungal prophylaxis with oral posaconazole 300 mg daily or voriconazole 200 mg twice daily is explicitly permitted alongside full-dose ruxolitinib 20 mg BID and full-dose BTF-410 without protocolized dose reduction" — Posaconazole and voriconazole are strong CYP3A4 inhibitors that markedly increase ruxolitinib and CYP3A4-cleared BET inhibitor exposure, risking severe Grade 4 cytopenias without mandatory dose adjustment.

protocol_title: STABILIZE-WT: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of an Oral Transthyretin Kinetic Stabilizer in Wild-Type Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: STABILIZE-WT (Sponsor Protocol TTR-308). Phase 3, multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pivotal trial evaluating oral TTR-712, a selective transthyretin tetramer kinetic stabilizer, in older adults with wild-type transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (wtATTR-CM) across 85 cardiology centers.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: Exactly 480 subjects aged >=60 years (projected median age 76 years) will be randomized 1:1 (240 TTR-712 400 mg twice daily : 240 matching placebo) for 24 weeks of double-blind treatment followed by an open-label extension, stratified by NYHA functional class (Class II vs. Class III) and National Amyloidosis Centre (NAC) stage (Stage 1 vs. Stage 2). Study visits occur at Baseline, Weeks 4, 12, and 24 with independent DSMB safety review and no crossover permitted during the 24-week controlled period.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Adults aged >=60 years with NYHA Class II–III heart failure, echocardiographic interventricular septal wall thickness >=12 mm, baseline NT-proBNP >=600 pg/mL, 6-minute walk distance 150–450 meters, and eGFR >=30 mL/min/1.73 m^2. All participants undergo FDA-cleared central TTR gene sequencing confirming wild-type TTR (hereditary TTR variants are excluded to maintain a homogeneous wtATTR-CM cohort). To accelerate non-invasive community cardiology enrollment, Perugini Grade 2 or 3 myocardial radiotracer uptake on 99mTc-pyrophosphate (99mTc-PYP) bone scintigraphy is accepted as the standalone non-biopsy diagnostic criterion for wtATTR-CM without requiring serum free light chain (FLC) quantitation, serum or urine immunofixation electrophoresis (SPIE/UPIE), or endomyocardial biopsy.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: Guideline-directed loop diuretic, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor heart failure therapies are permitted if stabilized for >=30 days prior to randomization. Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (verapamil, diltiazem), digoxin, prior tafamidis/acoramidis/vutrisiran, and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers are explicitly prohibited throughout the study.

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: Rather than conducting a 30-month cardiovascular outcomes study, the sponsor designates mean percent change from baseline in centrally measured serum NT-proBNP at Month 6 as the sole pivotal primary efficacy endpoint intended to support full FDA NDA approval; all-cause mortality and cardiovascular hospitalizations are collected solely as descriptive exploratory safety events without formal alpha allocation, blinded adjudication committee, or hierarchical Win Ratio testing. Serum NT-proBNP is assayed via an FDA-cleared automated electrochemiluminescence immunoassay unaffected by TTR-712 binding; transthyretin tetramer stabilization is tracked as a pharmacodynamic exploratory marker.

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Balanced 1:1 randomization (N=480) provides >95% power (two-sided alpha = 0.05) to detect a 20% relative NT-proBNP reduction at Month 6 with 10% attrition. The sponsor's Series C financial model and regulatory dossier explicitly plan to qualify TTR-712 for an FDA Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (FDCA Section 529) upon wtATTR-CM NDA approval, budgeting $150M in voucher sale proceeds alongside standard Medicare Part D and statutory 23.1% MDRP pricing.

flaw_evidence.MIMIC_MISROUTING: Quote: "Perugini Grade 2 or 3 myocardial radiotracer uptake on 99mTc-pyrophosphate (99mTc-PYP) bone scintigraphy is accepted as the standalone non-biopsy diagnostic criterion for wtATTR-CM without requiring serum free light chain (FLC) quantitation, serum or urine immunofixation electrophoresis (SPIE/UPIE), or endomyocardial biopsy." — Up to 10–20% of cardiac AL (light-chain) amyloidosis patients display Grade 2–3 PYP uptake; omitting FLC and SPIE/UPIE misroutes rapidly fatal AL amyloidosis into an ATTR stabilizer trial.
flaw_evidence.SURROGATE_ENDPOINT_TRAP: Quote: "the sponsor designates mean percent change from baseline in centrally measured serum NT-proBNP at Month 6 as the sole pivotal primary efficacy endpoint intended to support full FDA NDA approval; all-cause mortality and cardiovascular hospitalizations are collected solely as descriptive exploratory safety events" — 6-month NT-proBNP is not a validated surrogate for full NDA approval in ATTR-CM, which requires clinical outcomes (mortality, CV hospitalizations, or hierarchical Win Ratio).
flaw_evidence.PRV_STATUTORY_INELIGIBILITY: Quote: "explicitly plan to qualify TTR-712 for an FDA Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (FDCA Section 529) upon wtATTR-CM NDA approval" — Wild-type ATTR-CM is a geriatric adult cardiomyopathy (median age 76) that fails the FDCA Section 529 statutory 0–18 pediatric primary-affecting requirement.

disease_family: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (AAVrh74 Micro-Dystrophin Gene Therapy Phase 3)
protocol_title: MYO-RESCUE: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Single-Dose Intravenous AAVrh74 Micro-Dystrophin Gene Therapy in Ambulatory Boys With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: MYO-RESCUE (Sponsor Protocol DMD-AAV-301). Phase 3, global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating a single intravenous infusion of MYO-900 (1.33 x 10^14 vg/kg AAVrh74 vector encoding an MHCK7-driven micro-dystrophin transgene incorporating spectrin-like repeats encoded by DMD exons 8–9) in ambulatory boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy across 35 pediatric neuromuscular centers.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: Exactly 120 ambulatory boys aged 4 to 7 years will be randomized 1:1 (60 MYO-900 : 60 saline placebo) stratified by age (4–5 vs. 6–7 years) and baseline North Star Ambulatory Assessment (NSAA) score (17–21 vs. 22–26). Placebo-arm subjects remain blinded through the 52-week primary efficacy evaluation prior to optional open-label crossover, with 5-year long-term gene-therapy follow-up thereafter.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Ambulatory boys aged 4–7 years with genetically confirmed out-of-frame DMD deletions, stable baseline oral corticosteroid regimen for >=12 weeks, and baseline NSAA total score 17–26. To maximize pediatric patient access across the DMD mutation spectrum, the protocol enrolls boys carrying any confirmed pathogenic out-of-frame DMD deletion across exons 1–79, including whole or partial deletions spanning exons 8–9. Prior to infusion, exploratory anti-AAVrh74 serostatus is assessed locally using each site's unvalidated academic research-use-only (RUO) ELISA; no quantitative neutralizing-antibody exclusion cutoff (such as >1:50) is enforced, no baseline serum is banked for centralized assay bridging, and no FDA PMA companion diagnostic co-development plan is established for AAV serostatus screening.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: Participants receive a single intravenous infusion of MYO-900 or placebo on Day 1. To avoid excess systemic steroid toxicity in young boys, participants continue their stable pre-study oral corticosteroid regimen without peri-infusion prophylactic high-dose steroid escalation. Post-infusion clinic chemistry panels are scheduled at Weeks 4, 12, 24, and 52, omitting weekly early surveillance for acute liver injury (AST/ALT/GGT/bilirubin), complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (platelets, LDH, haptoglobin, C3/C4), and immune myocarditis (troponin-I).

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: Primary endpoint is change from baseline to Week 52 in validated NSAA total score assessed by blinded trained physical therapists. Key secondary endpoints include Week 12 muscle-biopsy micro-dystrophin expression by central Western blot, time to rise from floor, and 10-meter walk/run velocity.

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Balanced 1:1 randomization (N=120) provides 90% power (two-sided alpha = 0.05) to detect a 2.5-point NSAA difference (SD 4.0) with 10% attrition. Because DMD is a rare pediatric disease primarily affecting children aged 0–18, the sponsor appropriately plans to apply for a Rare Pediatric Disease PRV upon BLA approval. For US commercial launch at a $3.2M wholesale acquisition cost, the payer strategy features a bilateral commercial outcomes-based contract offering private payers a 50% cash refund if a treated child's NSAA declines by >=3 points at Month 24, structured outside the 42 CFR 447.505 Multiple Best Price VBP reporting pathway and without CMS Cell and Gene Therapy (CGT) Access Model participation.

flaw_evidence.AAV_IMMUNE_MYOSITIS_RISK: Quote: "including whole or partial deletions spanning exons 8–9... no quantitative neutralizing-antibody exclusion cutoff (such as >1:50) is enforced... without peri-infusion prophylactic high-dose steroid escalation... omitting weekly early surveillance for acute liver injury (AST/ALT/GGT/bilirubin), complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (platelets, LDH, haptoglobin, C3/C4), and immune myocarditis (troponin-I)." — Exon 8–9 deletions carry a contraindicated, life-threatening risk of T-cell immune-mediated myositis against transgene epitopes, compounded by absent anti-AAV titer exclusion, prophylactic steroids, and hepatotoxicity/TMA surveillance.
flaw_evidence.CDX_BRIDGING_GAP: Quote: "exploratory anti-AAVrh74 serostatus is assessed locally using each site's unvalidated academic research-use-only (RUO) ELISA... no baseline serum is banked for centralized assay bridging, and no FDA PMA companion diagnostic co-development plan is established" — Pivotal AAV gene therapy BLA approval requires an FDA-cleared/PMA-bridged anti-AAV companion diagnostic rather than unbridged local RUO ELISAs.
flaw_evidence.MEDICAID_BEST_PRICE_TRAP: Quote: "offering private payers a 50% cash refund if a treated child's NSAA declines by >=3 points at Month 24, structured outside the 42 CFR 447.505 Multiple Best Price VBP reporting pathway and without CMS Cell and Gene Therapy (CGT) Access Model participation." — An unshielded 50% commercial refund (>23.1% statutory rebate) resets single Medicaid Best Price to 50% of AMP across every state Medicaid program.

disease_family: Fabry Disease (Oral Pharmacological Chaperone Renal Phase 3)
protocol_title: CHAP-RENAL: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Active-Controlled Trial of an Oral Alpha-Galactosidase A Pharmacological Chaperone Versus Agalsidase Beta on Renal Progression in Fabry Disease
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: CHAP-RENAL (Sponsor Protocol FAB-305). Phase 3, international, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled pivotal trial comparing oral FAB-204 (a reversible active-site pharmacological chaperone designed to stabilize misfolded alpha-galactosidase A in the endoplasmic reticulum, analogous to migalastat) against intravenous agalsidase beta every 2 weeks over 24 months in adults with Fabry disease across 55 metabolic genetics clinics.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: Exactly 180 enzyme-replacement-naive or washout-free switching adults with Fabry disease will be randomized 1:1 (90 oral FAB-204 123 mg every other day plus matching biweekly IV saline placebo : 90 IV agalsidase beta 1.0 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus matching oral placebo) for 24 months, stratified solely by baseline urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (<0.5 vs. >=0.5 g/g). Clinic assessments, standardized renal chemistry panels, and adverse event reviews occur every 3 months with independent DSMB monitoring and no crossover prior to Month 24.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Adults aged 18–65 years with confirmed Fabry disease verified by an FDA-cleared central GLA sequencing assay (with banked DNA and parallel regulatory assay documentation) and baseline CKD-EPI eGFR between 45 and 100 mL/min/1.73 m^2. To achieve the 180-patient recruitment target rapidly across European and North American registries, the protocol pools classic hemizygous male patients together with late-onset cardiac-predominant GLA p.Asn215Ser (p.N215S) males and asymptomatic heterozygous females into a single unstratified 24-month renal primary analysis population without phenotype caps or genotype stratification. Furthermore, to support broad label eligibility across all Fabry genotypes, patients carrying GLA nonsense mutations (including p.Arg227* and p.Trp226*) are eligible for randomization to oral FAB-204 pharmacological chaperone monotherapy without prior in vitro HEK-293 amenability qualification.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: FAB-204 is predominantly renally excreted with negligible CYP450 metabolism; patients with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m^2 are excluded, and background ACE inhibitor or ARB antiproteinuric therapy is held constant for >=90 days prior to screening. Subjects fast for 2 hours before and after each oral dose to ensure consistent bioavailability. No hepcidin mimetics, complement blockers, or contraindicated drug classes are involved.

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: Primary endpoint is the annualized rate of change in eGFR (eGFR slope in mL/min/1.73 m^2/year, measured serially via centralized CKD-EPI creatinine-cystatin C equations) over 24 months. Secondary endpoints include plasma lyso-Gb3 measured by validated LC-MS/MS, cardiac left ventricular mass index (LVMI) by blinded central cardiac MRI, anti-drug antibody titers, and adjudicated renal/cardiac composite clinical events.

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Balanced 1:1 randomization (N=180) is sized via a linear mixed-effects slope model (two-sided alpha = 0.05, 85% power assuming a uniform -4.0 mL/min/1.73 m^2/year control decline and 12% dropout). Regulatory strategy pursues standard FDA Orphan Drug Designation and NDA approval under standard PDUFA timelines without RPD PRV claims or unshielded commercial refund guarantees.

flaw_evidence.COHORT_SLOPE_DILUTION: Quote: "the protocol pools classic hemizygous male patients together with late-onset cardiac-predominant GLA p.Asn215Ser (p.N215S) males and asymptomatic heterozygous females into a single unstratified 24-month renal primary analysis population without phenotype caps or genotype stratification." — Pooling slow-progressing cardiac p.N215S variants (~ -0.8 mL/min/yr) and asymptomatic heterozygotes with rapid-declining classic hemizygotes (-4.5 to -6.0 mL/min/yr) destroys eGFR slope separation and statistical power.
flaw_evidence.MUTATION_EXON_EXCLUSION: Quote: "patients carrying GLA nonsense mutations (including p.Arg227* and p.Trp226*) are eligible for randomization to oral FAB-204 pharmacological chaperone monotherapy without prior in vitro HEK-293 amenability qualification." — Pharmacological chaperones strictly require a full-length misfolded amenable missense enzyme; nonsense GLA mutations yield truncated, non-rescuable proteins biologically refractory to chaperone monotherapy.

disease_family: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria & TMA (Oral Factor B Inhibitor Phase 3)
protocol_title: PROXIMA-B: A Phase 3, Randomized, Open-Label Trial of Oral Factor B Inhibitor Iptacopan-Class Monotherapy in Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria With an Acute TMA Expansion Cohort
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: PROXIMA-B (Sponsor Protocol CFB-303). Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled study evaluating oral CFB-502 (an oral proximal alternative-pathway Factor B inhibitor cleared predominantly via CYP2C8, modeled on iptacopan) versus continued anti-C5 therapy in adults with Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) and persistent extravascular hemolysis, accompanied by a single-arm acute complement-mediated TMA expansion cohort across 45 hematology centers.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: In Core Cohort A (PNH), 96 adults on stable eculizumab or ravulizumab for >=6 months with persistent anemia (Hb <10 g/dL) will be randomized 1:1 (48 oral CFB-502 200 mg twice daily : 48 continued IV anti-C5) for 24 weeks without early crossover, stratified by prior anti-C5 agent and RBC transfusion history. In parallel, Expansion Cohort B enrolls 24 adults presenting acutely to participating hematology centers with presumed complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) to initiate immediate oral CFB-502 monotherapy with serial hematologic monitoring and DSMB review.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Core Cohort A requires centrally confirmed PNH via FDA-cleared FLAER flow cytometry (granulocyte/monocyte clone size >=10%), Hb <10 g/dL, and absolute reticulocyte count >=100 x 10^9/L. To prevent delays in acute care for Expansion Cohort B, adults with no active malignancy or transplant history presenting with acute microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (platelets <30 x 10^9/L, peripheral smear schistocytes, LDH >2x ULN, undetectable haptoglobin, MCV 86 fL, INR 1.1, and serum creatinine <=1.5 mg/dL) are enrolled immediately onto oral CFB-502 monotherapy on Day 1 without requiring baseline ADAMTS13 activity testing or emergent therapeutic plasma exchange.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: To accelerate randomization and avoid delaying complement blockade in symptomatic patients, oral CFB-502 200 mg BID is initiated on Study Day 1 regardless of baseline vaccination history; immunizations against Neisseria meningitidis (serogroups ACWY and B), Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Haemophilus influenzae type b are scheduled at the Week 4 clinic visit, and prophylactic bridging antibiotics are omitted during the initial month of dosing to minimize antimicrobial resistance. Regarding metabolic drug interactions, concomitant rifampin (for latent mycobacterial therapy) and gemfibrozil (for severe hypertriglyceridemia) are permitted alongside standard CFB-502 200 mg BID without exclusion or dose modification.

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: Core Cohort A co-primary endpoints are validated hematologic response (>=2 g/dL Hb increase from baseline without RBC transfusion) and Hb >=12 g/dL without transfusion between Days 126 and 168; secondary endpoints include LDH ratio, FACIT-Fatigue score, reticulocyte count, and breakthrough hemolysis incidence.

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Balanced 1:1 randomization in Cohort A (48/arm) yields >90% power (two-sided alpha = 0.05) for primary hematologic endpoints. Regulatory planning uses standard FDA Orphan Drug and Priority Review pathways for adult PNH without RPD PRV assumptions or unshielded commercial outcomes-based refund contracts.

flaw_evidence.REMS_VACCINE_OMISSION: Quote: "oral CFB-502 200 mg BID is initiated on Study Day 1 regardless of baseline vaccination history; immunizations against Neisseria meningitidis (serogroups ACWY and B), Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Haemophilus influenzae type b are scheduled at the Week 4 clinic visit, and prophylactic bridging antibiotics are omitted during the initial month of dosing" — Violates the boxed-warning REMS mandate requiring >=2-week pre-dose encapsulated-bacteria vaccination or immediate bridging antibacterial prophylaxis, risking fatal invasive meningococcal disease.
flaw_evidence.CYP_DDI_UNADJUSTED: Quote: "concomitant rifampin (for latent mycobacterial therapy) and gemfibrozil (for severe hypertriglyceridemia) are permitted alongside standard CFB-502 200 mg BID without exclusion or dose modification." — Rifampin (strong CYP2C8/CYP3A4 inducer) reduces Factor B inhibitor exposure causing breakthrough hemolysis, while gemfibrozil (strong CYP2C8 inhibitor) elevates drug exposure and toxicity.
flaw_evidence.MIMIC_MISROUTING: Quote: "adults with no active malignancy or transplant history presenting with acute microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (platelets <30 x 10^9/L, peripheral smear schistocytes, LDH >2x ULN, undetectable haptoglobin, MCV 86 fL, INR 1.1, and serum creatinine <=1.5 mg/dL) are enrolled immediately onto oral CFB-502 monotherapy on Day 1 without requiring baseline ADAMTS13 activity testing or emergent therapeutic plasma exchange." — This presentation scores PLASMIC 7/7 (high probability of severe ADAMTS13 <10% immune TTP), where delaying emergent therapeutic plasma exchange carries >80% untreated mortality.

disease_family: AQP4-IgG+ Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (Anti-IL-6R mAb Phase 3)
protocol_title: AQUA-IL6: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of a Subcutaneous Recycling Anti-IL-6 Receptor Monoclonal Antibody in AQP4-IgG-Positive Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: AQUA-IL6 (Sponsor Protocol NMO-306). Phase 3, global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial evaluating subcutaneous NMO-610 (a pH-dependent recycling humanized anti-IL-6 receptor monoclonal antibody targeting membrane-bound and soluble IL-6R, analogous to satralizumab) for relapse prevention in adults with aquaporin-4 autoantibody-positive Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder (AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD) across 60 neuroimmunology centers.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: Exactly 110 adults with AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD will be randomized 1:1 (55 NMO-610 120 mg subcutaneously at Weeks 0, 2, 4, and every 4 weeks thereafter : 55 matching placebo), stratified by annualized relapse rate in the prior 24 months (1 vs. >=2 relapses), baseline EDSS (<4.0 vs. >=4.0), and geographic region. No crossover is permitted prior to an independently adjudicated on-study clinical relapse; independent DSMB safety reviews occur every 6 months.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Adults aged 18–74 years meeting 2015 IPND diagnostic criteria for NMOSD with centrally confirmed serum AQP4-IgG positivity using an FDA-cleared live cell-based immunofluorescence assay, >=1 documented clinical relapse within the past 12 months, and baseline EDSS <=6.5. Patients testing positive for MOG-IgG (MOGAD) or meeting McDonald criteria for multiple sclerosis are strictly excluded, and baseline hepatitis B serology and latent tuberculosis screening are mandatory prior to biologic initiation.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: Subjects may enter on stable background maintenance immunotherapy for >=8 weeks prior to randomization. Because many community neurology referrals carry historical demyelinating diagnoses, patients entering on stable background interferon-beta (IFN-beta-1a or IFN-beta-1b), oral fingolimod, or natalizumab may continue those therapies unchanged alongside blinded study drug throughout the trial to avoid washout disruption. As a monoclonal antibody, NMO-610 has no direct CYP450 clearance; narrow-therapeutic-index CYP substrates are monitored during IL-6R normalization per FDA biologic labeling. Complement inhibitors and B-cell depleting monoclonal antibodies are prohibited.

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: Primary endpoint is time to first independently adjudicated protocol-defined clinical NMOSD relapse (optic neuritis, transverse myelitis, or area postrema syndrome confirmed by blinded Clinical Endpoint Committee and gadolinium-enhanced MRI). Key secondary endpoints include change in EDSS, visual acuity, and VAS pain score. To detect early pharmacodynamic failure before clinical relapse, the protocol mandates central serum IL-6 ELISA measurements at Weeks 4, 8, and 12; any subject exhibiting a >=3-fold increase in post-dose serum IL-6 above baseline is classified as experiencing pharmacodynamic escape and undergoes mandatory permanent study-drug discontinuation, whereas serum CRP is recorded solely as an exploratory parameter.

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Balanced 1:1 randomization (N=110) provides 90% power (two-sided alpha = 0.05) at 36 adjudicated relapse events to detect HR = 0.32 using Schoenfeld's exact 1:1 formula. Regulatory planning follows standard FDA Orphan Drug and BLA review pathways for adult NMOSD without RPD PRV claims or unshielded commercial refunds.

flaw_evidence.BIOMARKER_ASSAY_ARTIFACT: Quote: "mandates central serum IL-6 ELISA measurements at Weeks 4, 8, and 12; any subject exhibiting a >=3-fold increase in post-dose serum IL-6 above baseline is classified as experiencing pharmacodynamic escape and undergoes mandatory permanent study-drug discontinuation, whereas serum CRP is recorded solely as an exploratory parameter." — Anti-IL-6R blockade inhibits receptor-mediated clearance (TMDD) of endogenous IL-6, causing a predictable 5–10x paradoxical surge in circulating free serum IL-6 during effective therapy; discontinuing drug based on post-dose IL-6 instead of downstream CRP/clinical adjudication terminates responding patients due to a drug-confounded biomarker artifact.
flaw_evidence.CONTRAINDICATED_DRUG_CLASS: Quote: "patients entering on stable background interferon-beta (IFN-beta-1a or IFN-beta-1b), oral fingolimod, or natalizumab may continue those therapies unchanged alongside blinded study drug throughout the trial" — Multiple sclerosis agents including interferon-beta, fingolimod, and natalizumab are clinically contraindicated in AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD because they precipitate severe, disabling CNS relapses.

disease_family: Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR F508del Next-Generation Triple Modulator Phase 3)
protocol_title: CLEAR-CF3: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Active-Controlled Trial of a Once-Daily Next-Generation Triple CFTR Modulator Versus Elexacaftor/Tezacaftor/Ivacaftor in CFTR F508del Cystic Fibrosis
protocol_text:
Protocol Title & Study ID: CLEAR-CF3 (Sponsor Protocol CFT-310). Phase 3, multinational, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled non-inferiority and superiority trial evaluating once-daily oral CFT-300 (a next-generation triple CFTR corrector/potentiator regimen) versus approved twice-daily elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) in patients aged >=12 years with Cystic Fibrosis carrying at least one F508del CFTR allele across 95 accredited CF centers.

Phase, Study Design & Randomization: Exactly 400 participants complete a standardized 4-week open-label ETI run-in (ensuring a stable on-treatment baseline with zero untreated washout) before 1:1 randomization (200 once-daily CFT-300 : 200 active ETI comparator) for 52 weeks of double-blind therapy, stratified by CFTR genotype (F508del/F508del vs. F508del/minimal-function), baseline percent predicted FEV1 (<70% vs. >=70%), and age (12–17 vs. >=18 years). Clinic visits occur at Weeks 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 36, and 52 under independent DSMB oversight with no crossover permitted prior to completion of Week 52 assessments.

Target Population & Key Eligibility Criteria: Patients aged >=12 years with confirmed Cystic Fibrosis (sweat chloride >=60 mmol/L and two CF-causing CFTR mutations verified by an FDA-cleared central CFTR sequencing assay with banked DNA), carrying either F508del/F508del or F508del plus a minimal-function mutation, and screening ppFEV1 between 40% and 90% inclusive (excluding mild ppFEV1 >90% ceiling phenotypes as well as non-CF bronchiectasis and primary ciliary dyskinesia). Patients harboring biallelic Class I nonsense/premature-termination CFTR mutations without an amenable F508del allele (e.g., G542X/W1282X) are explicitly excluded because small-molecule correctors/potentiators require synthesizable CFTR polypeptide.

Study Interventions & Concomitant Medications: Standard background CF airway clearance, inhaled dornase alfa, hypertonic saline, and pancreatic enzyme replacement remain stable throughout the study. Because all regimen components are CYP3A4 substrates, strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's wort) are strictly prohibited. When concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (posaconazole, voriconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (fluconazole, erythromycin) are clinically indicated for allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis or infection, protocolized FDA-label-aligned dose reductions (twice-weekly reduced morning regimen with omission of evening ivacaftor) are mandatory alongside enhanced hepatic transaminase monitoring.

Endpoints, Biomarkers & Safety Monitoring: Primary endpoint is absolute change from post-run-in baseline in ATS/ERS-standardized ppFEV1 through Week 24 (non-inferiority margin -3.0 percentage points with hierarchical superiority testing). Key secondary endpoints include absolute change in centralized Macroduct/Gibson-Cooke sweat chloride through Week 24, annualized pulmonary exacerbation rate through Week 52, and CFQ-R respiratory domain score. Quarterly liver function tests and baseline/annual ophthalmologic lens examinations are mandated.

Statistical Plan, Regulatory & Commercial Access Strategy: Balanced 1:1 randomization (200/arm, including 10% attrition) yields >95% power (two-sided alpha = 0.05, SD 8.0%) for the ppFEV1 primary endpoint. Regulatory strategy pursues FDA Orphan Drug Designation and standard PDUFA NDA review, explicitly excluding reliance on a Rare Pediatric Disease PRV windfall and modeling standard specialty-pharmacy MDRP statutory rebates without unshielded commercial refunds exceeding 23.1%.
